statement: The equation $x^{2}+2kx+3k=0$ has real roots. Find the range of possible values of $k$.
solution:
For real roots the discriminant must be non-negative:
$$\Delta=(2k)^{2}-4(1)(3k)=4k^{2}-12k=4k(k-3)\ge0.$$
This holds when $k\le0$ or $k\ge3$.
hints: Real roots require the discriminant to be at least zero.
